# Codebase Onboarding

Curated by Skill Harbor: a systematic method for analyzing an unfamiliar codebase and producing a structured onboarding guide, built for developers joining a new project or setting up an AI coding agent in an existing repo for the first time. It works in phases: first a fast reconnaissance that gathers signals without reading every file (package manifests, framework fingerprints, entry points, directory snapshot, config and tooling detection, test layout), then an architecture mapping step that identifies the tech stack, data flow, and key conventions, and finally the generation of a guide plus a starter CLAUDE.md so the next session starts with context instead of rediscovery. Designed around the questions a newcomer actually asks: where does execution start, where does state live, how do I run the tests, what are the unwritten rules. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: guidance and analysis, it produces documents rather than modifying your code; it needs access to the repo (a local checkout or enough of the tree pasted in) to do the reconnaissance phase properly. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
